We're now validating it on real patient records and excited to try it out more broadly.” “Argon is doing a great job at understanding what people actually mean. Customers collect endless signals that they don't know what to do with. Argon consistently scored amongst the top in our evals for building charts that help visualize the solutions for customers. It's also meaningfully persistent about finding those kinds of needle in a haystack answers that are valuable to customers.”Curtis LiuCTO, Amplitude “Gemini 4 represents a step change in what AI can accomplish in real-world science. We've seen it reason through complex experimental data, from cellular imaging to mass spectrometry, and make subtle findings that traditionally require expert scientists to identify. On our Scientific Agent Benchmark, Gemini 4 was at the frontier across most tasks, including our hardest: ranking the clinical risk between two drugs.”Alex CabreraFounding Engineer, Axiom Bio “Gemini 4 Argon is at the frontier of enterprise knowledge work, achieving a 14% improvement in accuracy compared to Gemini 3.1 Pro. In Box’s evaluation, Argon connected evidence across the full set of documents, including details embedded in figures, and carried multi-step analyses through to complete answers. This is especially valuable in data analysis and in technical fields like healthcare and life sciences, where teams need to find and interpret information across many kinds of source material.”Yashodha BhavnaniVP of AI Products at Box “By integrating Gemini 4 into our 3D spatial reconstruction engine, we turn everyday video into articulated, physics-ready 3D scenes in seconds instead of hours. Across our benchmarks, Gemini outperformed every model we tested — cutting runtime nearly 100× and token usage by 90%, unlocking physics ready and watertight 3D asset creation for our customers.”Andrew CarrCo-founder and Chief Scientist, Cartwheel “Early impressions from Gemini 4 are very strong: for long-running tasks across these workflows, it completed successfully 100% of the time in our evals, maintaining context and running through multiple tools across impressive spans. Its depth of reasoning delivers significantly higher, clearer output. Performing in-depth reasoning for domain-specific tasks without detailed prior logic or instructions is something we’ve never seen with any model in its class before.”Gopal SrinivasanGlobal AI and Data Lead, Deloitte “On our core financial analysis benchmarks, which span building multi-year financial statements straight from SEC filings to valuing companies with complex capital structures and announced acquisitions, Gemini 4 matched our analyst-built reference models on more than 99% of figures. Performance on our most complex workflows was at the frontier in a majority of tasks. We're excited to keep building with Gemini 4 at Kepler.”Glenn LeBlancSoftware Engineer, Kepler “To help legal professionals achieve more with Lexis+ with Protégé, we continuously evaluate AI models as part of the multi-model approach behind the LexisNexis Legal Intelligence Engine. In preliminary evaluations, Gemini 4 Argon demonstrated strong performance across legal knowledge, drafting, and analysis tasks, including identifying relevant citations and improving contract reviews, complaint analyses, and research memos.”Min ChenChief AI Officer, LexisNexis Legal & Professional “In early testing, Gemini 4 Argon stood out by connecting dates, documents, and financial calculations with legal precedents to develop highly substantive arguments. In one evaluation, it actually surpassed our human expert's answer key by surfacing a legally relevant detail we had missed. This demonstrates AI’s potential to help professionals uncover crucial details and bring a more complete understanding to complex cases.”Caio PeronaCEO, MinutalA “In Qualia, our autonomous AI researcher, Gemini 4 Argon has been a standout in our evaluations for both capability and efficiency. On our internal benchmarks of complex, multi-step research tasks, it performs at the frontier while completing our evals 1.5x faster than peer models at a quarter of the cost per task. It excelled at coming up with novel ideas and identifying non-obvious insights about the problem, helping it maintain a clear research vision over long horizons, something today's models struggle with.”Trenton ChangChief Scientist, Quadrillion “Gemini 4 impressed us with the quality of its responses in our early evaluations. We’ve fully integrated Argon into Roboflow so developers and enterprises can leverage its high precision detection and text extraction to inspect products, track inventory, and guide machines.”Brad DwyerCo-founder and CTO of Roboflow Quantum computingNuclear fusionRare disease diagnosisEnzyme design To demonstrate these capabilities in action, we tested Argon’s ability to learn an out of distribution physical skill simply by watching. In an internal test, Argon watched a raw video of a human playing cornhole, mapped the spatial coordinates of the environment, and calculated the required whole-body joint movements. It then autonomously built the simulation code. When transferred onto Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid, the robot quickly sank seven consecutive shots in a real-world trial. comments.author: gertlabs
comments.textRawHtml:
We evaluated Gemini 4 Argon in 100 unsaturated, competitive and cooperative coding environments. It's roughly in between Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 in our testing, so it's maybe 2 months behind the frontier.

Google's major releases have usually done pretty well on our benchmarks because they're good at hard problems and open-ended decision making (with a well specified prompt), which obviously doesn't always translate to user experience. In particular, older Google models struggled to work efficiently in a harness. They seem to have solved that with Argon.

We did see a new problem which I hope they can fix. This is the first near-frontier model we've caught in infinite reasoning loops in a long time. We also saw a few examples of it failing to properly delineate reasoning blocks, so it has a higher failure rate than its competitors.

My overall impression is that Argon is a near-frontier model for engineering design, code analysis, and chat. It definitely has the intelligence to be a competitive coding assistant product, but a good coding assistant needs to be polished, so I hope they can clean up the CoT bugs.

Data at https://gertlabs.com/rankings

children.textRawHtml: At this point I'm interested less in how well a model can code, but more in how well it can produce code that humans can understand.

children.author: booty
children.textRawHtml:
I have had pretty decent success instructing OpenAI/Anthropic models to do this. By default, they don't care too much about human readability (which is understandable) but they're amenable to instruction.

- Basic style/linter rules (so you don't get 200-line functions, etc) paired w/ instructing your agent how to use them goes a long way (e.g., a sane rubocop.yml in your repo, plus a note in AGENTS.md telling the agents how to run rubocop, or whatever makes sense for your language) - I have a code review skill that specifically calls out human-readability concerns such as making sure that identifier names represent their contents and intended use

The other key IME is that you need to make readability/refactoring passes outside of a particular pull request. When working on a specific branch the LLMs will be somewhat myopic, and do stuff that looks pretty good in isolation, but when you zoom out and look at the bigger picture it's kind of a mess - for example, often they'll duplicate some code that existed elsewhere.

The LLMs are also pretty good at generating Mermaid charts and tracing execution flows, which is a great way to understand code. It doesn't help them to produce more readable code but it helps me to understand code I'm unfamiliar with.

children.author: brna-2
children.textRawHtml:
I think we are coming to a point where we are at a sweet spot for immersive human collaboration work.

Yep, it will generate what ever you ask for but if you want to have some sort of exploratory work, immersion, feeling of ownership and genuinely a connection with the things you are building - a part the build loop should belong to you.

Maybe this is an attachment of people who built things in other ways. Maybe the perceived value of applications will drop to near 0 and you will end up having all in one apps or voice wants like to a star trek replicator. Fun things are coming, but humanity will need to adjust hard - best case scenario.

children.author: simpaticoder
children.textRawHtml: I agree, and I find it sad that so many people and companies are in a rush to take the human out of the loop. But for agentic/human hybrids not even all of those work out well - and the error modes have more to do with the "alignment" of the human. That is, humans with strong knowledge, an aesthetic sense for structure, strong curiosity - those humans do well in this loop. Humans that just want to "make money" using the LLM as a slave, interacting with it as little as possible, taking no interest in what it does (bad company leadership in miniature) get poor outputs. When the human is an invested, knowledgeable curator of code, someone who has a vision that goes beyond the external, you get some really great stuff.

> This is the first near-frontier model we've caught in infinite reasoning loops in a long time

Depends on where you draw the line for "near frontier model", but the current leading open-weights model, MiMo-v2.6, has exactly this problem. They released a fix on Hugging Face[1], but as of two days ago the model available via Xiaomi's own API still sticks in reasoning loops.

[1] https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD
